evidence: src/controllers/cardsController.ts: create, activate, getStatement, blockCard, unblockCard and createVirtual each destructure req.body/req.params, call cardServices.* and respond with send/sendStatus.

src/controllers/paymentsController.ts: buyOnPointOfSale and buyOnline destructure typed bodies (BuyOnPOSBody, BuyOnlineBody), call paymentServices.insertPayment/insertOnlinePayment and respond with sendStatus(200).
src/controllers/rechargeController.ts: recharge destructures cardId and amount, calls rechargeService.recharge and responds with sendStatus(200).
None of the files contains validation or business rules, so nothing is duplicated across controllers; all logic goes through the services layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files are thin Express request handlers in the same style. Each one pulls values from req, calls one service function and sends a status code. They cover one concern (HTTP adaptation for card features) and hold no business logic, so no rule or invariant is duplicated across them. No file goes around the service abstraction. One small inconsistency: only paymentsController.ts declares typed request-body interfaces, while the other two destructure req.body untyped. That is a style difference, not a split in concerns or a duplicated rule. The services and schemas importing those interfaces is a dependency-direction issue and is out of scope.
